<!-- Generated by HelpShortcuts from the application's own key bindings (drumscore-editor d16a23d5). Do not edit by hand: change the generator. -->

Each key is shown as it is on a Mac, and as it is on Windows and Linux. `Cmd` is the Command key, and `Option` is the key Windows and Linux call `Alt`. Where the Mac column says `Ctrl`, it means the Control key and not `Cmd`: the rest keys and the text tag key are the ones to watch. Where Linux differs from Windows, a note under the table says how. An empty box means there is no key on that system.

The keys that write and change music work only while the music has the keyboard. If a key does nothing, click in the music first. On Windows the menus and windows also have access keys, the underlined letters that `Alt` shows, which are not listed here.

## Files and windows

| To | Mac | Windows and Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Make a new score | `Cmd+N` | `Ctrl+N` |
| Open a score | `Cmd+O` | `Ctrl+O` |
| Open one of the nine most recent scores, by its place in `Open Recent` | `Cmd+1` to `Cmd+9` | `Alt+1` to `Alt+9` |
| Save the score | `Cmd+S` | `Ctrl+S` |
| Print the score | `Cmd+P` | `Ctrl+P` |
| Close the score | `Cmd+W` | `Ctrl+W` or `Ctrl+F4` |
| Show the next open score | `Ctrl+Tab` | `Ctrl+Tab` |
| Show the open score before this one | `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` | `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` |
| Minimise the window | `Cmd+M` |  |
| Open `Settings` | `Cmd+,` |  |
| Open this guide |  | `F1` |
| Quit | `Cmd+Q` |  |
| Close the `Create New Score` window without making a score |  | `Esc` |
| In the `Create New Score` window, move from one tune type to another | `Left`, `Right`, `Up`, `Down` | `Left`, `Right`, `Up`, `Down` |
| In `Settings`, move from one appearance to the next | `Left`, `Right` | `Left`, `Right` |

On Linux these differ from Windows:

- Open one of the nine most recent scores, by its place in `Open Recent`: `Ctrl+1` to `Ctrl+9`
- Close the score: `Ctrl+W`
- Quit: `Ctrl+Q`

On Linux `Ctrl+2` to `Ctrl+9` also make a tuplet, and while the music has the keyboard that is what they do. Click outside the music first, or use the menu, to open a recent score there.

## Undo, copy and paste

`Undo` and `Redo` also work while a header or footer is being arranged.

| To | Mac | Windows and Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Undo | `Cmd+Z` | `Ctrl+Z` |
| Redo | `Cmd+Shift+Z` | `Ctrl+Y` |
| Redo, while the music has the keyboard | `Cmd+Y` or `Cmd+Shift+Z` | `Ctrl+Y` or `Ctrl+Shift+Z` |
| Cut what is selected | `Cmd+X` | `Ctrl+X` |
| Copy what is selected | `Cmd+C` | `Ctrl+C` |
| Paste at the caret | `Cmd+V` | `Ctrl+V` |
| Delete what is selected | `Backspace` or `Delete` | `Backspace` or `Delete` |

On Linux these differ from Windows:

- Redo: `Ctrl+Shift+Z`

## Moving the caret

| To | Mac | Windows and Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Left a little | `Left` | `Left` |
| Right a little | `Right` | `Right` |
| To the line above | `Up` | `Up` |
| To the line below | `Down` | `Down` |
| To the start of the next bar | `Space` | `Space` |
| To the next bar | `Tab` | `Tab` |
| To the previous bar | `Shift+Tab` | `Shift+Tab` |
| Open the right-click menu from the keyboard | `Menu` or `Shift+F10` | `Menu` or `Shift+F10` |
| Leave the music for the next part of the window | `F6` | `F6` |
| Leave the music for the part of the window before it | `Shift+F6` | `Shift+F6` |

## Writing notes and rests

The letter is the length of the note. The letter alone writes a left-hand note, with `Shift` a right-hand note, and with `Ctrl` a rest. It is written at the caret.

| To | Mac | Windows and Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Left-hand semibreve | `A` | `A` |
| Left-hand minim | `S` | `S` |
| Left-hand crotchet | `D` | `D` |
| Left-hand quaver | `F` | `F` |
| Left-hand semiquaver | `G` | `G` |
| Left-hand demisemiquaver | `H` | `H` |
| Right-hand semibreve | `Shift+A` | `Shift+A` |
| Right-hand minim | `Shift+S` | `Shift+S` |
| Right-hand crotchet | `Shift+D` | `Shift+D` |
| Right-hand quaver | `Shift+F` | `Shift+F` |
| Right-hand semiquaver | `Shift+G` | `Shift+G` |
| Right-hand demisemiquaver | `Shift+H` | `Shift+H` |
| Semibreve rest | `Ctrl+A` |  |
| Minim rest | `Ctrl+S` |  |
| Crotchet rest | `Ctrl+D` | `Ctrl+D` |
| Quaver rest | `Ctrl+F` | `Ctrl+F` |
| Semiquaver rest | `Ctrl+G` | `Ctrl+G` |
| Demisemiquaver rest | `Ctrl+H` | `Ctrl+H` |
| A Swiss ruff by itself, with no main note, for the left hand | `I` | `I` |
| The same for the right hand | `Shift+I` | `Shift+I` |
| Make the selected notes and rests one step shorter | `Shift+N` | `Shift+N` |
| Make the selected notes and rests one step longer | `Shift+M` | `Shift+M` |
| Swap the hand of the selected notes | `Shift+K` | `Shift+K` |

On Windows and Linux `Ctrl+A` is `Select All` and `Ctrl+S` is `Save`, so there is no key there for a semibreve rest or a minim rest. Use the toolbox buttons for those.

## Selecting

While a bar or a part is selected the note keys do not write: the first press lets the selection go.

| To | Mac | Windows and Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Select one more note to the left, or one fewer | `Shift+Left` | `Shift+Left` |
| Select one more note to the right, or one fewer | `Shift+Right` | `Shift+Right` |
| Carry the selection on to the line above | `Shift+Up` | `Shift+Up` |
| Carry the selection on to the line below | `Shift+Down` | `Shift+Down` |
| Select everything in the music area the caret is in | `Cmd+A` | `Ctrl+A` |
| Widen the selection: from notes to their bar, from a bar to its part | `Cmd+Up` | `Ctrl+Up` |
| Narrow it again: from a part to a bar, from a bar to its notes | `Cmd+Down` | `Ctrl+Down` |
| With a bar or a part selected, select the next one | `Tab` | `Tab` |
| With a bar or a part selected, select the one before | `Shift+Tab` | `Shift+Tab` |
| Select nothing | `Esc` | `Esc` |

## Marks on notes

These act on the notes that are selected. Press the key again to take the mark off.

| To | Mac | Windows and Linux |
|---|---|---|
| A flam | `Z` | `Z` |
| A drag | `X` | `X` |
| An open drag | `C` | `C` |
| A Swiss ruff | `V` | `V` |
| A ruff (also known as a rough) | `B` | `B` |
| An accent | `Y` | `Y` |
| A heavy accent | `Shift+Y` | `Shift+Y` |
| A staccato | `Shift+O` | `Shift+O` |
| A marcato | `Option+O` | `Alt+O` |
| A backstick | `Shift+B` | `Shift+B` |
| A roll | `R` | `R` |
| Step a roll through one, two and three slashes | `Shift+R` | `Shift+R` |
| A dot. On a pair of notes: dot the first and halve the second | `.` | `.` |
| A cut. On a pair of notes: halve the first and dot the second | `-` | `-` |
| A double dot | `Shift+.` | `Shift+.` |

## Beams, ties, tuplets and other groups

Select the notes first. A group runs from the first selected note to the last.

| To | Mac | Windows and Linux |
|---|---|---|
| A beam to the note before, or break it | `L` | `L` |
| A single beam only | `Shift+L` | `Shift+L` |
| A tie | `T` | `T` |
| A tuplet of that many: `3` is the triplet | `2` to `9` or `Ctrl+2` to `Ctrl+9` | `2` to `9` or `Ctrl+2` to `Ctrl+9` |
| A crescendo | `K` | `K` |
| A diminuendo | `M` | `M` |
| Unison | `U` | `U` |
| Unison that stops at the note | `Shift+U` | `Shift+U` |

## Highlight pens

A pen highlights the notes and rests that are selected. Press the key again to take the highlight off.

| To | Mac | Windows and Linux |
|---|---|---|
| `Pen 1` to `Pen 10` | `Shift+0` to `Shift+9` | `Shift+0` to `Shift+9` |

## A tenor on five lines

These are for a tenor stave drawn on five lines, where a note is written at a pitch.

| To | Mac | Windows and Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Set the pitch for the next note one higher | `W` | `W` |
| Set it one lower | `Q` | `Q` |
| Add a note-head at that pitch to the selected note, or take it out | `E` | `E` |
| Move the selected notes up | `Shift+W` | `Shift+W` |
| Move the selected notes down | `Shift+Q` | `Shift+Q` |

## Moving and spacing

| To | Mac | Windows and Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Nudge the selection to the left | `Option+Shift+Left` | `Ctrl+Shift+Left` |
| Nudge the selection to the right | `Option+Shift+Right` | `Ctrl+Shift+Right` |
| Squeeze: space the selected run of notes out | `Cmd+Right` | `Ctrl+Right` |
| Squeeze: draw the selected run of notes in | `Cmd+Left` | `Ctrl+Left` |
| Beautify | `Option+B` | `Alt+B` |

On Linux these differ from Windows:

- Nudge the selection to the left: `Alt+Shift+Left`
- Nudge the selection to the right: `Alt+Shift+Right`

## Text and text tags

| To | Mac | Windows and Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Put a text tag on the selection, or take it off | `Ctrl+T` | `Ctrl+T` |

### While words are being typed

| To | Mac | Windows and Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Keep what you typed | `Enter` | `Enter` |
| Abandon it | `Esc` | `Esc` |
| Put a text tag above its note, or below it | `Option+Up`, `Option+Down` | `Alt+Up`, `Alt+Down` |
| Move left or right by a letter | `Left`, `Right` | `Left`, `Right` |
| Move left or right by a word | `Option+Left`, `Option+Right` | `Ctrl+Left`, `Ctrl+Right` |
| Move to the start or the end of the words | `Home`, `End` | `Home`, `End` |
| Select as you move | `Shift` with any of those | `Shift` with any of those |
| Select all the words | `Cmd+A` | `Ctrl+A` |
| Cut, copy, paste | `Cmd+X`, `Cmd+C`, `Cmd+V` | `Ctrl+X`, `Ctrl+C`, `Ctrl+V` |
| Delete the letter before the caret, or the one after it | `Backspace`, `Delete` | `Backspace`, `Delete` |

## Arranging a header or footer

Double-click a header or footer to arrange it. Until you finish, the keys that write and change music do nothing.

| To | Mac | Windows and Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Nudge the selected piece | `Option+Shift` with an arrow key | `Ctrl+Shift` with an arrow key |
| Delete the selected piece | `Delete` or `Backspace` | `Delete` or `Backspace` |
| Finish arranging | `Esc` | `Esc` |

On Linux these differ from Windows:

- Nudge the selected piece: `Alt+Shift` with an arrow key

## Music areas on a page arranged by hand

Click a music area's outline to hold it.

| To | Mac | Windows and Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Nudge the music area | `Option+Shift` with an arrow key | `Ctrl+Shift` with an arrow key |
| Delete the music area | `Backspace` or `Delete` | `Backspace` or `Delete` |

On Linux these differ from Windows:

- Nudge the music area: `Alt+Shift` with an arrow key

Any other key that acts on the music lets go of the music area and does nothing else.

## View and zoom

| To | Mac | Windows and Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Actual size | `Cmd+0` | `Ctrl+0` |
| Zoom in | `Cmd+=` or `Cmd+Numpad +` | `Ctrl+=` or `Ctrl+Numpad +` |
| Zoom out | `Cmd+-` or `Cmd+Numpad -` | `Ctrl+-` or `Ctrl+Numpad -` |

## Playing and recording

| To | Mac | Windows and Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Abandon a recording during its count-in or its take | `Esc` | `Esc` |
| Clear the practice section, once nothing is selected | `Esc` | `Esc` |

## The Rudiments panel

These act while a list in the `Rudiments` panel has the keyboard.

| To | Mac | Windows and Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Remove the selected phrase from its library | `Backspace` or `Delete` | `Backspace` or `Delete` |
